description: SOT-23 to 0.1-inch single-row adapter; right-angle header included
notes: Order separately from Chip Quik / Proto-Advantage; no verified DigiKey SKU. USD1.09 each, USD3.27 for three, in stock when checked 2026-10-16. Inspect actual copper routes and check continuity before applying power. No current rating for the adapter is inferred from the MOSFET rating. This separate purchase is not included in generated min.csv.

description: Multimeter, plug-in jumpers, insulated wire, soldering tools and heat-shrink for PoC
notes: Both configurations use a 64-row solderless breadboard and suitable plug-in jumpers, plus suitably rated insulated wires soldered directly from J0 pin 1 to strip +. Minimum additionally requires soldering each AO3400A onto a SIPK03-1 adapter and installing its included header. Disconnect all power before soldering; insulate and strain-relieve power joints. Check the assembled adapter pin mapping with a meter before inserting it into the breadboard. Best practice links the left/right +12 V and ground rails at the top and bridges all four midpoint breaks. Minimum feeds the left +12 V rail from J0 with a58 to L+58 and the lower-left ground rail with a60 to L-60. B1 bridges the left +12 V midpoint break; B4 bridges the right ground midpoint break. A ground cross-link joins L-39 to R-39. Both right +12 V rail halves and the upper-left ground rail are unused; there are no driver-ground links. Nano VIN connects at a15 to L+15; minimum Nano GND connects at j12 to R-12. Strip + bypasses breadboard rails. Minimum has no driver supply branches.

description: 12 V common-positive RGB strip; planned 160 inches total
notes: Both configurations: start with one marked cut segment; maximum 25 cm gives 3.6 W/0.30 A at full white, approximately 0.10 A per color, plus controller draw. Verify actual current; cut only at marked pads. Strip + connects directly to J0 pin 1 via a soldered insulated wire; row 40 is unused. Best-practice strip leads: a41 green, a42 red, a43 blue. Minimum exposes the same color nets on J1/J2: pin 3 red, pin 4 green, pin 5 blue; pin 2 positive connects through soldered pigtails to J0.1. Return current still passes through breadboard contacts; the positive bypass does not increase the load limit. Full 160 inches=4.064 m/58.52 W/4.88 A is for later rated wiring; higher-current MOSFETs do not make the breadboard suitable for that load. Sections connect in parallel to like pads.

description: Breadboard-friendly 2.1 mm DC barrel jack; thin-pin type
notes: Both configurations retain J0; replaces panel-mount jack for PoC. DigiKey CP-102AH-ND; CAD 1.15 checked 2026-10-16, before tax/shipping. Included in generated min.csv. Manufacturer specifies breadboard-friendly pins: https://www.adafruit.com/product/373 . Minimum: centre-positive pin 1 at c58, sleeve ground pin 2 at c60, and unused switched contact pin 3 at e59. Best practice retains pin 1 at b58, pin 2 at b60, and unused pin 3 at d59. Minimum Nano supply jumpers connect a58 to L+58 and a60 to L-60. Solder the strip-positive wire to the actual pin 1 terminal, not a breadboard hole such as a58 or e58. Insulate and strain-relieve the joint; remove the jack from the breadboard before soldering. Gently form pins if needed; verify contact identity with unplugged meter. Drawing: https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/21mmdcjackDatasheet.pdf

description: Best-practice and minimum short-strip prototypes with direct strip-positive wiring
notes: Both retain J0 and parallel Nano VIN/strip supply branches. Strip + is soldered directly to J0 pin 1, bypassing positive breadboard contacts; strip returns still use breadboard contacts. Row 40 is unused. The load limit remains 25 cm/0.30 A total. Minimum uses three AO3400A MOSFETs on SIPK03-1 adapters, three 2.2 kohm series gate resistors, and two parallel RJ-11 jacks J1/J2. It omits gate drivers, added capacitors and pulldowns as requested; the gates can float during startup/reset. Use the default low-frequency PWM; these gate resistors are not intended for high-frequency switching. Best practice retains three IRFZ44NPBF MOSFETs, two TC4427A drivers, three driver-input pulldowns, three 100 ohm gate resistors, three gate-to-source pulldowns, driver 100 nF/4.7 uF bypass pairs, and optional C7. No F0/F1 holders or external J12 block in either PoC. Start with one strip segment, up to 25 cm after checking current. Full strip at low PWM brightness still has high-current pulses; do not use that as a substitute for a short load.
